title: Antibiotic resistance
examples: How does using antibiotics too much make bacteria stronger?
Can we predict when bacteria will become resistant?
What is the role of natural selection in this process?

explain.say: Today we will learn about antibiotic resistance in bacteria. This happens when bacteria become resistant to medicines. It is a process linked to natural selection.
Natural selection means nature selects the best suited organisms. In bacteria, this means the strongest ones survive. The medicine kills the weaker ones first.
Misuse of antibiotics means not taking them correctly. For example, stopping treatment too soon is a major problem. This allows the strongest bacteria to thrive.
A concrete example is a skin infection. If you take antibiotics only for a few days, some bacteria might not die. These survivors pass on their resistance genes.
In everyday life, this happens when people treat colds with antibiotics. Antibiotics only work on bacteria, not viruses. This misuse speeds up resistance development.
A common mistake is thinking that one dose of antibiotics is enough. You must always follow the doctor's full instructions. Never share antibiotics with others.

faq.q: Why do bacteria become resistant to antibiotics?
faq.a: Resistance develops because of natural selection acting on bacteria populations. When antibiotics are used, they kill the weaker bacteria, allowing naturally resistant ones to survive and multiply.
asks: How does natural selection cause resistance?
What makes bacteria stronger against drugs?

faq.q: Is it true that antibiotics only work on bacteria?
faq.a: Yes, antibiotics are designed to target and kill bacteria specifically. They have no effect on viruses, so taking them for a cold will not help.
asks: What kind of germs do antibiotics fight?

faq.q: What is the best way to prevent antibiotic resistance?
faq.a: The best way is responsible use of antibiotics. This means only taking them when prescribed and finishing the entire course even if you feel better.
asks: How can we stop bacteria from becoming resistant?
What should I do after taking antibiotics?

faq.a: Yes, the process can happen quite rapidly once antibiotics are used improperly. Bacteria reproduce very quickly, allowing resistance genes to spread quickly through the population.
asks: Is it a slow process or fast?

faq.q: If I feel better, should I stop taking my antibiotics?
faq.a: No, you must never stop taking antibiotics just because you feel better. Stopping early leaves the strongest bacteria alive to develop resistance.
asks: Can I stop medicine when I feel fine?
Is it safe to stop antibiotics early?

facts: Antibiotics are medicines used to treat bacterial infections.
Natural selection favors bacteria that possess resistance genes.
Misusing antibiotics, like stopping early, accelerates resistance.
Antibiotics do not treat viral infections like the common cold.

quiz.say: A patient takes only half of their prescribed antibiotics.

options.show: The body fighting off the remaining germs.
options.say: The body fighting off the remaining germs.

quiz.why: Stopping early means weaker bacteria are killed, but the strongest ones have time to multiply without full treatment.

wrong.0: While resistance develops, the drug is not useless instantly; it requires time and selection.
wrong.1: The body's immune system might struggle against the new, resistant strain.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the patient feels better, but the remaining bacteria are still alive.

quiz.say: Which factor primarily drives the development of resistance?

options.show: The immune system failing to respond.
options.say: The immune system failing to respond.

options.show: The overuse of antibiotics in farming.
options.say: The overuse of antibiotics in farming.

quiz.why: Antibiotics create a selective environment, allowing only the pre-existing resistant bacteria to survive and dominate.

wrong.0: Immune failure is a symptom, not the primary cause of the bacterial resistance mechanism.
wrong.2: Mutation happens, but the antibiotic is what selects for the beneficial mutations.
wrong.3: While this is a major factor, the core biological mechanism is the selection process itself.

options.show: They should be used as a preventative measure.
options.say: They should be used as a preventative measure.

options.show: They are always safe to take.
options.say: They are always safe to take.

options.show: Not effective because colds are viral.
options.say: Not effective because colds are viral.

quiz.why: Antibiotics target bacterial cell walls and processes, which viruses do not have.

wrong.0: Preventative use is misuse and contributes to resistance.
wrong.1: They can cause side effects and promote resistance if misused.
wrong.3: This is incorrect because antibiotics only work on bacteria, not viruses causing colds.
